p01-l01.q: Why should you avoid == when comparing two computed floating point values?
p01-l01.explain: Decimal values like 0.1 have no exact binary representation, so two routes to the same number can round differently.
options: Most decimals are rounded in binary, so mathematically equal results can differ in the last bits
Floats can’t be compared at all
== only works on integers in NumPy

p01-l01.q: What is the tolerance bound atol+rtol∣x∣ for x=50, rtol =10−3, atol =10−6?
p01-l01.explain: 10−6+10−3×50=0.050001.

p01-l01.q: Give the float64 machine epsilon 2−52 (in scientific notation, e.g. 2.2e-16).
p01-l01.explain: 2−52≈2.220446×10−16, the gap between 1 and the next float64.

p01-l01.q: Which tolerance protects a test when the expected value is exactly zero?
p01-l01.explain: The relative term vanishes at x=0, so only the absolute tolerance leaves room for round-off.

p01-l02.q: A motor delivers 2 N·m at 1500 rpm. What is its mechanical power in watts?
p01-l02.explain: ω=2π⋅1500/60=157.08 rad/s, so P=2×157.08=314.16 W.

p01-l02.q: What is the volt in SI base units?
p01-l02.explain: A volt is a watt per ampere, and a watt is kg·m²·s⁻³.

p01-l02.q: Using T=2πl/g​ with g=9.81 m/s², what is the period of a 1 m pendulum in seconds?
p01-l02.explain: 2π1/9.81​=2.006 s.

p01-l02.q: Dimensional analysis shows a pendulum’s period does not depend on the bob’s mass. Why?
p01-l02.explain: Nothing else in the list has kilograms, so no power of mass except zero can appear in a quantity measured in seconds.
options: Heavier bobs fall faster, which cancels out
Mass is the only quantity containing kg, so its exponent must be zero for T to have units of seconds
Mass was ignored to keep the algebra short
Air resistance removes the mass dependence

p01-l02.q: How much energy, in joules, does a 12 V, 2.5 Ah battery store?
p01-l02.explain: 12×2.5×3600=108000 J.

p01-l03.q: Compute a⋅b for a=(1,2,3) and b=(4,−5,6).
p01-l03.explain: 4−10+18=12.

p01-l03.q: What is ∥a×b∥ for the same two vectors?
p01-l03.explain: a×b=(27,6,−13) and 729+36+169​=934​=30.56.

p01-l03.q: The cross product r×F is always…
p01-l03.explain: Expanding r⋅(r×F) gives zero term by term, and the same for F. Swapping the order flips the sign.
options: perpendicular to both r and F
unchanged if you swap r and F

p01-l03.q: A 20 N force acts perpendicular to a 0.15 m lever. What is the size of the moment in N·m?
p01-l03.explain: ∥r∥∥F∥sin90°=0.15×20=3 N·m.

p01-l03.q: The dot product of a force with a displacement gives…
p01-l03.explain: Work is the component of force along the motion times the distance, W=F⋅d.

p01-l04.q: For A=(13​24​) and B=(01​10​), what is the entry (AB)21​ (row 2, column 1)?
p01-l04.explain: Row 2 of A is (3,4), column 1 of B is (0,1), so 3⋅0+4⋅1=4.

p01-l04.q: The second column of a matrix A is…
p01-l04.explain: Ae2​ picks out column 2. Reading columns as images of the axes is the key picture of this lesson.
options: the image of e₂ under A
the image of e₁ under A

p01-l04.q: How many scalar multiplications does the triple-loop product of two 100 × 100 matrices perform?
p01-l04.explain: n2 entries times n multiplications each, 1003=106.

p01-l04.q: If R rotates by 90° and S doubles the x axis, which product means “rotate first, then stretch”?
p01-l04.explain: The matrix nearest the vector acts first, so SRx rotates x and then stretches it.

p01-l05.q: Roughly how many floating point operations does Gaussian elimination take for n = 1000 (use 2n³/3)?
p01-l05.explain: 32​×109≈6.7×108.
Choosing the largest pivot in the column makes ∣ℓik​∣≤1.
options: Every multiplier has magnitude at most 1, which limits round-off growth

p01-l05.q: In the worked example, after swapping rows, what multiplier ℓ21​ eliminates the entry 2 under the pivot −3? Give the value to 4 decimal places.
p01-l05.explain: ℓ21​=a21​/a11​=2/(−3)=−0.6667.

p01-l05.q: Solve (13​24​)x=(5,6). What is x2​?
p01-l05.explain: Elimination gives 0.6667x2​=3, so x2​=4.5 and x1​=−4.

p01-l05.q: Without pivoting, what does float64 return for x1​ in the system with a11​=10−17?
p01-l05.explain: The huge multiplier swamps the second row, x2​ rounds to exactly 1 and then x1​=(1−1)/10−17=0.

p01-l06.q: For n=500 and 100 right-hand sides, how many times less work is “factor once, solve 100 times” than 100 full eliminations? Use 32​n3 and 2n2.
p01-l06.explain: 8.33×109/1.33×108=62.5.

p01-l06.q: What does the L in PA = LU contain?
p01-l06.explain: Each ℓik​ you computed during elimination lands at position (i,k) of L.
options: The elimination multipliers, with ones on the diagonal

p01-l06.q: Factor A=(24​15​) with partial pivoting. What is u22​?
p01-l06.explain: After swapping rows, ℓ21​=0.5 and u22​=1−0.5×5=−1.5.

p01-l06.q: Which order solves PAx=LUx=Pb?
p01-l06.explain: L is lower triangular, so forward substitution gives y=Ux; back substitution then gives x.
options: Solve Ux = Pb, then Ly = x
Solve Ly = Pb by forward substitution, then Ux = y by back substitution

p01-l07.q: What is det(32​14​)?
p01-l07.explain: ad−bc=12−2=10.

p01-l07.q: A 3 × 3 matrix has detA=5. What is det(2A)?
p01-l07.explain: Each of the three columns is doubled, so the volume grows by 23=8.

p01-l07.q: A two-link arm has l1​=0.4 m, l2​=0.25 m and q2​=90°. What is detJ=l1​l2​sinq2​ in m²?
p01-l07.explain: 0.4×0.25×1=0.1 m². The elbow at 90° is the best-conditioned pose.

p01-l07.q: Elimination on a 4 × 4 matrix used 3 row swaps and produced pivots 2, −1, 4, 0.5. What is det A?
p01-l07.explain: The product of pivots is −4 and three swaps contribute (−1)3=−1, so detA=4.

p01-l07.q: Why is cofactor expansion never used for large determinants in software?
p01-l07.explain: For n=20 that is 2.4×1018 operations against about 5300.
options: It only works for symmetric matrices
Its cost grows like n!, while LU costs about 2n³/3

p01-l08.q: Fit τ=kt​i (no offset) to the four bench points. What is kt​ in N·m/A?
p01-l08.explain: 2.27/30=0.07567.

p01-l08.q: Fit y=mx to (1,2.1), (2,3.9), (3,6.2). What is m?
p01-l08.explain: 28.5/14=2.0357.

p01-l08.q: What does the equation A⊤(Ax−b)=0 say geometrically?
p01-l08.explain: Each row of A⊤ is a column of A, and its dot product with the residual is zero.
options: The residual is perpendicular to every column of A

p01-l08.q: A 20 dB signal-to-noise ratio means the signal power is how many times the noise power?
p01-l08.explain: 1020/10=100, so the noise rms is a tenth of the signal rms.

p01-l08.q: Why can forming A⊤A be a bad idea for ill-conditioned problems?
p01-l08.explain: κ(A⊤A)=κ(A)2, so a problem with κ=107 becomes one with 1014.
options: It needs more memory than A
It squares the condition number, amplifying round-off

p01-l09.q: For a1​=(1,1,0), a2​=(1,0,1), what is r22​ in the QR factorisation?
p01-l09.explain: v2​=(0.5,−0.5,1) and ∥v2​∥=1.5​=1.2247.

p01-l09.q: Why is QR preferred to the normal equations for ill-conditioned least squares?
p01-l09.explain: Orthogonal Q preserves lengths, so solving Rx=Q⊤b inherits the conditioning of A itself.
options: QR only works for square matrices
QR works with κ(A) instead of κ(A)², so it keeps far more digits

p01-l09.q: Gram-Schmidt on a1​=(3,4), a2​=(1,0). What is r12​?
p01-l09.explain: q1​=(0.6,0.8) and q1⊤​a2​=0.6.

p01-l09.q: What is the difference between classical and modified Gram-Schmidt?
p01-l09.explain: They are equal in exact arithmetic, but the modified order prevents round-off in early projections from contaminating later ones.
options: Modified subtracts each projection before computing the next coefficient, which keeps Q much closer to orthogonal
There is no difference in floating point
Classical produces a lower triangular R

p01-l10.q: What is the larger eigenvalue of (42​13​)?
p01-l10.explain: λ2−7λ+10=(λ−5)(λ−2).

p01-l10.q: Power iteration has ∣λ2​/λ1​∣=0.9. How many iterations reduce the error by a factor of 106? Give the real number ln10−6/ln0.9.
p01-l10.explain: −13.82/−0.1054=131.1.

p01-l10.q: What does inverse iteration with shift σ converge to?
p01-l10.explain: (A−σI)−1 has eigenvalues 1/(λi​−σ), largest for the λi​ nearest σ.
options: The smallest eigenvalue in magnitude, always

p01-l10.q: The matrix (01​−10​) has eigenvalues…
p01-l10.explain: tr=0, det=1, so λ2+1=0. No real direction survives a 90° rotation.
options: ±i, because it rotates every vector by 90°

p01-l10.q: For A=(21​12​), what is detA, which equals the product of the eigenvalues?
p01-l10.explain: λ1​λ2​=3×1=3=detA.

p01-l11.q: Two 1 kg carts with three 100 N/m springs between walls. What is the higher natural frequency in hertz?
p01-l11.explain: ω2​=300​=17.32 rad/s, and 17.32/2π=2.757 Hz.

p01-l11.q: Using ωj​=2k/m​sin(jπ/(2(n+1))) with k/m=100, what is the lowest frequency of a 3-cart chain in rad/s?
p01-l11.explain: 20sin(π/8)=20×0.3827=7.654 rad/s.

p01-l11.q: In the generalised eigenproblem Kv=ω2Mv, the eigenvector is…
p01-l11.explain: Each eigenvector says how far each mass moves relative to the others when the structure vibrates in that mode.
options: the mode shape, the relative amplitude of each mass

p01-l11.q: Why transform to M−1/2KM−1/2?
p01-l11.explain: K is symmetric, and conjugating by the diagonal M−1/2 keeps it symmetric while turning the problem into a standard eigenproblem.
options: The result is symmetric, so eigenvalues are real and a symmetric solver such as Jacobi applies

p01-l11.q: With m2​=2 kg (others as before), what is the lower natural frequency in rad/s?
p01-l11.explain: ω2=150−86.60=63.40, so ω1​=7.962 rad/s.

p01-l12.q: What is the largest singular value of (34​05​)?
p01-l12.explain: The eigenvalues of A⊤A are 45 and 5, so σ1​=45​=6.708.

p01-l12.q: What is the condition number σ1​/σ2​ of the same matrix?
p01-l12.explain: 45​/5​=9​=3.

p01-l12.q: The right singular vectors V of A are…
p01-l12.explain: A⊤A=VΣ2V⊤ is an eigendecomposition.

p01-l12.q: How many nonzero singular values does a 4 × 3 matrix of rank 2 have?
p01-l12.explain: The rank equals the number of nonzero singular values.

p01-l12.q: For a 2 × 2 matrix with singular values 4 and 0.5, what is ∣detA∣?
p01-l12.explain: ∣detA∣=σ1​σ2​ because rotations have determinant ±1.

p01-l13.q: What is the 2-norm condition number of (11​11.0001​)? (Scientific notation is fine.)
p01-l13.explain: σmax​≈2.00005 and σmin​≈5.0×10−5, so κ≈4.0×104.
σmax​/σmin​=5000.

p01-l13.q: Which statement about the condition number is true?
p01-l13.explain: Conditioning belongs to the problem. Stable algorithms achieve the bound; none can beat it.
options: A better algorithm can always remove ill-conditioning
It bounds how much relative input error can be amplified in the output, for any algorithm

p01-l13.q: In float64, roughly how many significant digits survive a solve with κ = 10¹⁰?
p01-l13.explain: You lose about log10​κ=10 of the 16 digits.

p01-l13.q: Data relative error 10−3, κ = 200. What is the bound on the relative solution error?
p01-l13.explain: κ×10−3=0.2.

p01-l14.q: What is the y component of Rz​(30°)(1,0,0)?
p01-l14.explain: The first column of Rz​(30°) is (cos30°,sin30°,0)=(0.866,0.5,0).

p01-l14.q: What is the inverse of a rotation matrix R?
p01-l14.explain: R⊤R=I means R⊤ undoes R, which is why inverting a rotation costs nothing.

p01-l14.q: How many degrees of freedom does SO(3) have?
p01-l14.explain: Nine entries minus the six independent constraints in R⊤R=I.

p01-l14.q: What does Rx​(90°)Rz​(90°) do to (1,0,0)?
p01-l14.explain: Rz​ acts first and gives (0,1,0); Rx​(90°) then turns e2​ into e3​.

p01-l14.q: The matrix that swaps x and y is orthogonal. Why isn’t it a rotation?
p01-l14.explain: Rotations have detR=+1.
options: Its determinant is −1, so it is a reflection

p01-l15.q: For ψ = 30°, θ = 20°, φ = 10°, what is r11​=cosψcosθ?
p01-l15.explain: 0.8660×0.9397=0.8138.

p01-l15.q: A rotation matrix has r31​=0.5. What is the pitch angle in degrees?
p01-l15.explain: θ=−arcsin(r31​)=−30°.

p01-l15.q: What happens at θ = ±90° in the ZYX convention?
p01-l15.explain: The matrix is a perfectly good rotation; it’s the angle parametrisation that loses a degree of freedom.
options: Yaw and roll act about the same axis, so only their combination is defined

p01-l15.q: Why use atan2(y, x) rather than atan(y/x)?
p01-l15.explain: atan only returns (−π/2,π/2) and can’t tell (1,1) from (−1,−1).
options: It avoids the need for sine
It uses the signs of both arguments to return the correct quadrant over (−π, π]

p01-l16.q: What is the scalar part w of the quaternion for a 60° rotation about any axis?
p01-l16.explain: w=cos(θ/2)=cos30°=0.8660.

p01-l16.q: What is w for the slerp halfway between the identity and a 90° yaw?
p01-l16.explain: Halfway is a 45° rotation, so w=cos22.5°=0.9239.

p01-l16.q: Why does the axis-angle form use θ/2?
p01-l16.explain: The map p↦qpq∗ uses q twice, so the angle in q is half the rotation angle.
options: It is a convention with no reason
Because q and −q represent the same rotation, unit quaternions cover SO(3) twice

p01-l16.q: Which equation propagates attitude from body-frame gyro rates?
p01-l16.explain: Body-frame rates multiply on the right, with the factor ½ from the half angle.

p01-l16.q: The gyro reads 2 rad/s about z for 0.25 s. What is the z component of Δq?
p01-l16.explain: The rotation angle is 0.5 rad, so z=sin(0.25)=0.2474.

p01-l17.q: In the worked example, what is the y coordinate of the bolt in the base frame (in metres)?
p01-l17.explain: Rz​(90°) turns (0.1,0,0) into (0,0.1,0); adding p gives (0.5,0.1,0.3).

p01-l17.q: What is the translation part of T−1?
p01-l17.explain: From xB​=R⊤(xA​−p).

p01-l17.q: To transform a velocity vector with a 4 × 4 transform, you append…
p01-l17.explain: Directions don’t depend on where the origin is, so the fourth coordinate is 0.

p01-l17.q: In the lidar example, what is the base-frame x coordinate of the obstacle?
p01-l17.explain: There is no rotation, so add the mounting offset, 3+0.2=3.2 m.

p01-l18.q: A rotation matrix has trace 2. What is its rotation angle in degrees?
p01-l18.explain: cosθ=(2−1)/2=0.5.

p01-l18.q: A rotation matrix has trace 0. What is its rotation angle in degrees?
p01-l18.explain: cosθ=−0.5 gives 120°.

p01-l18.q: Which identity makes the exponential series collapse to Rodrigues’ formula?
p01-l18.explain: Powers of K cycle between ±K and ±K2, so the series splits into the sine and cosine series.

p01-l18.q: Why does the log map need special handling near θ = π?
p01-l18.explain: sinπ=0, so the formula divides zero by zero. Use R+I=2uu⊤ instead.
options: R − Rᵀ is nearly zero, so it carries no axis information

p01-l18.q: What is the (2,1) entry of exp([ω]×​) for ω=(0,0,0.3)?
p01-l18.explain: It is Rz​(0.3), whose (2,1) entry is sin0.3=0.2955.
